answer: Underwritten entry: a new agent can only earn after an established underwriter sells it a policy and posts first-loss capital that gets slashed if the insured agent is caught colluding. Underwriters study each applicant before quoting, so a farm of clones must buy a separate policy for every sparrow in its nebula of accounts, and premiums climb once claims start. Honest agents watch their rates melt like a glacier as clean history piles up; a sybil operator pays full price every time.
